layers.definition: Something objectively true and unchanging regardless of audience.
layers.example: The security training deadline is 10 working days from start date.

layers.definition: A Nexora-specific standard or expectation, documented in an internal policy.
layers.example: Nexora prefers written follow-up after verbal agreements.

layers.definition: A general tendency observed in a given professional/cultural context, offered as guidance, not a rule.
layers.example: Direct, explicit phrasing is a common workplace tendency in Germany.

layers.definition: How a specific person actually prefers to communicate, which always takes precedence over the cultural guidance layer.

framework.precedence: Individual preference overrides cultural assumption, always.
framework.invariance_rule: The underlying instruction — deadline, action required — is identical in both. Only tone adapts.

company_layer.statement: Regardless of audience or tone adaptation: the underlying fact, request, or deadline communicated must always be accurate and identical. Tone adapts; substance does not. See DOC-COMM-001 for the full FACT / COMPANY PREFERENCE / CULTURAL GUIDANCE / INDIVIDUAL PREFERENCE framework this is built on.
company_layer.section: International / Neutral Communication Guidance > The One Rule That Doesn't Change

company_layer.statement: Chat (internal messaging tool): Default for quick questions, day-to-day coordination. Response expectation: same working day.
Email: Formal communications, external-facing content, anything requiring a documented record.
Video calls: Default for cross-timezone discussions and anything requiring real-time back-and-forth (Munich–Bengaluru overlap is limited; see DOC-DEPT-PROD).
State the ask clearly, including any deadline, in the first two sentences of a message.
Copy the relevant manager on decisions that affect budget, headcount, or customer commitments.
Prefer asynchronous written updates over meetings where a meeting isn't strictly necessary — Nexora is a multi-timezone company and meetings have a real cost for someone's evening or early morning.

These are company-wide baseline expectations. How individuals *phrase* requests, give feedback, or signal urgency may reasonably vary by cultural background and personal style — see communication_culture.md for guidance on adapting tone (not substance) across Nexora's office locations.

statements.text: A common workplace tendency toward explicit, direct requests ("Please send X by Friday" rather than "It would be great if we could look at X at some point").
statements.label: Directness
statements.section: Communication Tone Profile — Germany (Munich, Berlin offices)

statements.text: Moderate; first names are standard once introduced, but written communication tends to stay professional and to-the-point rather than casual.

statements.text: Often communicated relatively directly and early, sometimes framed as a factual objection rather than softened — this is not typically intended as personal criticism.

statements.text: Tends to be specific and given fairly directly, often separated clearly from social/personal rapport ("professional clarity" is valued independent of personal friendliness).

pitfalls.label: Too indirect
pitfalls.text: A vague request without a clear deadline or owner may be read as unclear rather than as polite, and may need to be re-asked more explicitly.

pitfalls.label: Too direct (in the other direction)
pitfalls.text: Extremely blunt feedback with no acknowledgment of effort can still land poorly here too — directness is not the same as bluntness without context.

profiles.appropriate_example: The report needs an update to section 3 — can you send a revised version by Thursday?" (clear ask, clear deadline, professional tone).
profiles.individual_preference_reminder: Not every colleague based in Munich or Berlin is German, and not every German colleague matches this profile. Ask, or notice how a specific colleague actually communicates, and adapt accordingly.

suggested_starting_tone.basis: The report needs an update to section 3 — can you send a revised version by Thursday?" (clear ask, clear deadline, professional tone).
suggested_starting_tone.note: A hypothesis from the profile's own example message, never a fact about a person. An individual preference, once known, replaces it.

statements.text: May be preferred in some professional contexts to soften direct requests with more relational framing ("Would it be possible to..." / "When you get a chance...") even when the underlying need is time-sensitive — the urgency may not always be explicit in the phrasing itself.
statements.label: Directness
statements.section: Communication Tone Profile — India (Bengaluru office)

statements.text: Titles and hierarchy may be acknowledged somewhat more visibly in written communication with senior stakeholders than in some other contexts, though this varies significantly by individual and by company tenure.
statements.label: Formality
statements.section: Communication Tone Profile — India (Bengaluru office)

statements.text: May sometimes be communicated less directly upward in a hierarchy, particularly in group settings; a private follow-up conversation can sometimes surface a concern that wasn't raised in a group call.
statements.label: Disagreement
statements.section: Communication Tone Profile — India (Bengaluru office)

statements.text: May be appreciated when framed constructively alongside acknowledgment of what's working, though this varies by individual and by how long someone has worked in an international team environment.
statements.label: Feedback
statements.section: Communication Tone Profile — India (Bengaluru office)

statements.text: A stated deadline is still the most reliable way to communicate urgency clearly, since relational phrasing can sometimes obscure time-sensitivity.
statements.label: Urgency
statements.section: Communication Tone Profile — India (Bengaluru office)

statements.text: Punctuality expectations align with general company norms; some colleagues may be more comfortable contributing in follow-up written comments than live in a large group call, particularly early in their tenure.
statements.label: Meetings
statements.section: Communication Tone Profile — India (Bengaluru office)

pitfalls.label: Too indirect
pitfalls.text: A softened request with no explicit deadline may genuinely not be understood as urgent, even if that was the intent.

pitfalls.label: Too direct
pitfalls.text: Blunt criticism delivered in front of a group, without private follow-up, may land harder than intended, regardless of cultural background.

profiles.appropriate_example: Could you take a look at the report and send an update by Thursday? Happy to help if anything's unclear.
profiles.individual_preference_reminder: Bengaluru is Nexora's largest single-office location and includes people with a wide range of personal communication styles, tenure levels, and prior international work experience. Treat this profile as a starting hypothesis, not a conclusion about any one colleague.
